# Week9 Homework

:::{.callout-tip title="Problem 1"}
Modify one of the simpler functions (SecondFunction or similar), provide your own argument names, and modify the `message()`, `paste0` or `print()` functions to print a text style output. Generate a small vector of values, and iterate through your vector using one of the approaches we used.
:::

```{r}
MySecondFunction <- function(FastestCytometer){
    message("The Fastest Cytometer is the ", FastestCytometer)
}

MySecondFunction(FastestCytometer = "Attune")

Cytometers <- c("Attune", "Aurora", "FACSDiscover", "ID7000", "Xenith")
str(Cytometers)

MySecondFunction(FastestCytometer = Cytometers[1])

for (Name in Cytometers){
    MySecondFunction(FastestCytometer=Name)
}

```


:::{.callout-tip title="Problem 2"}
Using the initial framework for the CellConcentration function, retrieve several other keywords that are of interest, and incorporate them into the returned data.frame row. 
:::

```{r}
# Load Libraries
library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
```

```{r}
# Set Storage Folder, file paths
StorageLocation <- file.path("data") # Quarto Rendering path
fcs_files <- list.files(StorageLocation, pattern=".fcs", full.names=TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Create Gating Set
MyCytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, transformation=FALSE, truncate_max_range=FALSE)
MyGatingSet <- GatingSet(MyCytoset)
```

```{r}
# Apply Biexponential Transformation to the Data and check that it makes sense
MainDetectorsOnly <- c("V3-A", "B4-A", "R1-A")

Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144,
     pos=4.5, neg=2, widthBasis=-500)
MyBiexTransform <- transformerList(MainDetectorsOnly, Biexponential)
transform(MyGatingSet, MyBiexTransform)

ggcyto(MyGatingSet[[1]], subset="root",
 aes(x="V3-A", y="R1-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

ggcyto(MyGatingSet[[1]], subset="root",
 aes(x="V3-A", y="B4-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

ggcyto(MyGatingSet[[1]], subset="root",
 aes(x="R1-A", y="B4-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)
```

```{r}
# Create Gating Table
GatingTable <- tibble::tribble(
  ~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,           
  "CD45",       list("B4-A", "SSC-A"),            "root",     
  "CD19",       list("V3-A", "SSC-A"),            "CD45",   
  "CD14",       list("R1-A", "SSC-A"),            "CD45", 
  "TandNKcells",  list("V3-A", "SSC-A"),            "CD45",
)

# Create and apply gates
flowGate::gs_apply_gating_strategy(MyGatingSet, gating_strategy = GatingTable)
plot(MyGatingSet)

pData(MyGatingSet)$name
```


```{r}

# Create Functions

CellConcentration <- function(x, subset, dilutionMultiplier){
    Date <- keyword(x)$`$DATE`
    InstrumentSerial <- keyword(x)$`$CYTSN`
    TotalFileEvents <- keyword(x)$`$TOT`
    Specimen <- keyword(x)$GUID
    StartTime <- keyword(x)$`$BTIM`
    EndTime <- keyword(x)$`$ETIM`
    CD45_GainSetting <- keyword(x)$`$P43V`
    CD45_BitDepth <- keyword(x)$`$P43B`

    Volume <- keyword(x)$`$VOL`
    Volume <- as.numeric(Volume)

    EventsInTheGate <- gs_pop_get_data(x, subset)
    Cells <- nrow(EventsInTheGate)[[1]] #[[1]] since the output is in a list

    Concentration <- (Cells*1000)/Volume
    Concentration <- Concentration*dilutionMultiplier


Data <- data.frame(
        Date=Date,
        InstrumentSerial=InstrumentSerial,
        Specimen=Specimen,
        StartTime=StartTime,
        EndTime=EndTime,
        Volume=Volume, 
        Cells=Cells,
        Concentration=Concentration,
        CD45_GainSetting=CD45_GainSetting,
        CD45_BitDepth=CD45_BitDepth,
        TotalFileEvents=TotalFileEvents
        
        )

    return(Data)


}

purrr::map(.x=MyGatingSet[1], .f=CellConcentration, subset="root", dilutionMultiplier=1)

KeywordList <- purrr::map(.x=MyGatingSet[1], .f=CellConcentration, subset="root", dilutionMultiplier=1)
head(KeywordList[[1]],10000)

# Create a single data.frame containing all samples
KeywordTable <- purrr::map_dfr(
    MyGatingSet,
    CellConcentration,
    subset = "root",
    dilutionMultiplier =1
)

KeywordTable

# Export data.frame as CSV file
write.csv(KeywordTable, file = file.path("homeworks","Problem2.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
```


:::{.callout-tip title="Problem 3"}
For CellConcentration, we retrieved both start and end time. Look up information on `lubridate` package, convert these times to a time-style format, and from acquired volume derive uL/min at which each .fcs file was acquired. Did this vary at all across days?
:::

```{r}
#install.packages("lubridate")

library(lubridate)

CellConcentration <- function(x, subset, dilutionMultiplier){
    Date <- keyword(x)$`$DATE`
    InstrumentSerial <- keyword(x)$`$CYTSN`
    TotalFileEvents <- keyword(x)$`$TOT`
    Specimen <- keyword(x)$GUID
    StartTime <- keyword(x)$`$BTIM`
    EndTime <- keyword(x)$`$ETIM`
    CD45_GainSetting <- keyword(x)$`$P43V`
    CD45_BitDepth <- keyword(x)$`$P43B`

    Volume <- keyword(x)$`$VOL`
    Volume <- as.numeric(Volume)

    EventsInTheGate <- gs_pop_get_data(x, subset)
    Cells <- nrow(EventsInTheGate)[[1]] #[[1]] since the output is in a list

    Concentration <- (Cells*1000)/Volume
    Concentration <- Concentration*dilutionMultiplier

    StartDateTime <- strptime(
        paste(Date, StartTime),
        format = "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%OS"
    )

    EndDateTime <- strptime(
        paste(Date, EndTime),
        format = "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%OS"
    )

    AcquisitionMinutes <- as.numeric(
        difftime(
            EndDateTime,
            StartDateTime,
            units = "mins"
        )
    )

    AcquisitionRate <- AcquisitionMinutes/Volume


Data <- data.frame(
        Date=Date,
        InstrumentSerial=InstrumentSerial,
        Specimen=Specimen,
        StartTime=StartTime,
        EndTime=EndTime,
        Volume=Volume, 
        Cells=Cells,
        Concentration=Concentration,
        CD45_GainSetting=CD45_GainSetting,
        CD45_BitDepth=CD45_BitDepth,
        TotalFileEvents=TotalFileEvents,
        AcquisitionMinutes = AcquisitionMinutes,
        AcquisitionRate=AcquisitionRate

        
        )

    return(Data)
}


KeywordTable <- purrr::map_dfr(
    MyGatingSet,
    CellConcentration,
    subset = "root",
    dilutionMultiplier =1
)

KeywordTable
```

The acquisition rate in ul/min was very stable between acquisition dates.
